native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: See answer: PC1 (30.3% var) contrasts a prestige-accumulation pole (Cu&Au, decorated pottery, deposits/hoards, hatchets/swords, daggers, monument size/count, house size; positive) against a productive-craft pole (pottery form, axes/celts, amber, sickle; negative). Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE): all 5 slices NEGATIVE (mean -1.392, median -1.486, range -1.81..-0.59) - deep productive/craft regime, deepest at 3000 BCE. Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE): all 7 slices still NEGATIVE (mean -1.132, median -1.230, range -1.62..-0.42) - same regime, mildly less negative (+0.26 shift) with late-phase pulses (2700, 2300 BCE), never crossing zero; decisive positive PC1 comes later (~1900 BCE). Pollen-openness PC1 is a distinct axis (pollen taxa) that covaries positively (r=+0.73 with SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) but is not part of the capital PCA.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parse comma-decimal Z-columns; use capital.csv rows (BCE 4300..500, step -100) as the hundred-year time-slice matrix (verified identical to time_series CE%100==0 rows); 12 already-z-scored capital variables. 2) Correlation PCA (39x12): centered/scaled to unit variance; eigen-decomposition; PC1 = 30.33% variance. 3) Sign convention: orient so largest |loading| (ZCU_AU, Copper&Gold) is positive; loadings and scores flipped together (score = scaled X @ oriented eigenvector). 4) Phase stats for MN (3400-3000 BCE, 5 slices) and Younger Neolithic/SG (2900-2300 BCE, 7 slices): mean/median/min/max and sign; year-by-year transition deltas. 5) Robustness: repeat PCA on 37-slice subset (BCE 4100-500) and on 11 variables (drop ZSichel). 6) Pollen context: merge capital PC1 scores with pollen_openness SMOOTH_MEAN_100y and MEAN at shared century slices (n=36); Pearson correlation; per-phase means. Scripts: data/inspect_data.py (schema/quality checks) and analyze_capital_pca.py (main analysis); synth2.py (sign sanity check).

sub_hypo.context: Forms of capital during the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE).
sub_hypo.relations: Both prehistoric phases are primarily associated with negative scores on the first principal component derived from the individual forms-of-capital attributes.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.

sub_hypo.text: Capital PC1 explains 30.33% of variance and contrasts prestige accumulation with productive-craft capital.
sub_hypo.context: Correlation PCA of 12 already-z-scored capital variables across 39 century slices from 4300 to 500 BCE, centered and scaled to unit variance; PC1 is oriented so Copper and Gold, the largest absolute loading, is positive.
sub_hypo.relations: Copper and Gold, decorated pottery, deposits/hoards, hatchets/swords, daggers, monument size, monument count, and house size load positively on PC1; pottery form, axes/celts, amber, and sickle load negatively.

sub_hypo.text: The Middle Neolithic exhibits a consistently deep productive-craft regime, with its most negative capital PC1 score at 3000 BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Middle Neolithic, 3400–3000 BCE, comprising five century slices scored using the capital PCA fitted to 4300–500 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: All five derived capital PC1 scores are negative: mean -1.392, median -1.486, range -1.81 to -0.59. The minimum occurs at 3000 BCE.

sub_hypo.text: The Younger Neolithic remains in the productive-craft regime but is mildly less negative than the Middle Neolithic; positive capital PC1 emerges only later, around 1900 BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Younger Neolithic/SG, 2900–2300 BCE, comprising seven century slices, compared with the Middle Neolithic at 3400–3000 BCE and the later transition around 1900 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: All seven Younger Neolithic capital PC1 scores are negative: mean -1.132, median -1.230, range -1.62 to -0.42. The phase mean shifts upward by approximately 0.26 relative to the Middle Neolithic. Pulses at 2700 and 2300 BCE do not cross zero; decisive positive scores occur later, around 1900 BCE.

sub_hypo.text: Pollen-openness PC1 covaries positively with capital PC1 but represents a distinct pollen-taxa axis rather than a component of the capital PCA.
sub_hypo.context: Capital PC1 scores merged with pollen-openness data at 36 shared century slices; Pearson correlation with the 100-year-smoothed pollen measure.
sub_hypo.relations: Derived capital PC1 scores correlate positively with SMOOTH_MEAN_100y (Pearson r = +0.73). Pollen-openness variables are excluded from the capital PCA.

Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE): all 5 slices NEGATIVE (mean -1.392, median -1.486, range -1.81..-0.59) - deep productive/craft regime, deepest at 3000 BCE. Pollen-openness PC1 is a distinct axis (pollen taxa) that covaries positively (r=+0.73 with SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) but is not part of the capital PCA.
